raw_response:
I have been farming this land in Quzhou for 30 years, and I know what works here. My 13.1 mu is all going into cotton this year—it's what this soil is good for, and the market is steady. In spring, once the ground warms up in late April, I will rotary-till the fields to break up the stubble and weeds, then plant an improved cotton variety. I trust the improved seeds because they give reliable germination and decent resistance without the gamble of saving my own seed. For fertilizer, I will put down about 15 kg of nitrogen per mu, plus 5 kg of phosphorus and 8 kg of potassium—cotton is hungry when the bolls are setting, and my soil benefits from the potash. I have a well, so I will irrigate three times: once at planting to get the seedlings established, once at flowering in July when the heat hits, and once during peak boll development in August. I do not spray chemicals blindly, but I will keep four applications ready for the season—one early for aphids, and the others timed for bollworm and mites if they show up. With good weather and my experience, I expect to bring in around 270 kg per mu of seed cotton. Some of my family works off-farm, so I keep the plan simple and manageable without needing to hire much extra labor.
